## 1. The Conceptual Shift: Phase Space Systems & Matrix Exponentials

Linear systems $\dot{\mathbf{x}} = A \mathbf{x}$ are solved globally via the **matrix exponential** $e^{At}$. The Wronskian obeys the **Liouville-Ostrogradsky formula** $W(t) = W(t_0) \exp(\int \text{tr}(A) ds)$.

---

## 2. Numerical Computation: Matrix Exponential via Scaling & Squaring

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## Python 3
```python
import numpy as np

# Simple harmonic oscillator system A = [[0, 1], [-1, 0]]
A = np.array([[0.0, 1.0], [-1.0, 0.0]])
t = np.pi / 2.0
# exp(A * pi/2) = [[0, 1], [-1, 0]] rotated by 90 deg = [[0, 1], [-1, 0]]
# Using Taylor truncation
At = A * t
exp_At = np.eye(2) + At + (At@At)/2.0 + (At@At@At)/6.0 + (At@At@At@At)/24.0
print("Python 3: Truncated exp(A * pi/2):")
print(np.round(exp_At, 4))
```

## C++20
```cpp
#include <iostream>
#include <cmath>
#include <array>

int main() {
    // A = [[0, 1], [-1, 0]], t = pi/2
    // Exact exp(At) = [[cos(t), sin(t)], [-sin(t), cos(t)]]
    double t = M_PI / 2.0;
    double m00 = std::cos(t), m01 = std::sin(t);
    double m10 = -std::sin(t), m11 = std::cos(t);

    std::cout << "C++20:    exp(A * pi/2):\n";
    std::cout << "[" << m00 << ", " << m01 << "]\n[" << m10 << ", " << m11 << "]\n";
    return 0;
}
```

## Julia
```julia
using LinearAlgebra
A = [0.0 1.0; -1.0 0.0]
exp_At = exp(A * (pi / 2))
println("Julia:    exp(A * pi/2) = \n", round.(exp_At, digits=4))
```

## Modern Fortran
```fortran
program exp_mat
  implicit none
  real(8), parameter :: pi = 3.141592653589793d0
  real(8) :: t, m00, m01, m10, m11

  t = pi / 2.0d0
  m00 = cos(t); m01 = sin(t)
  m10 = -sin(t); m11 = cos(t)

  print '(A)', "Fortran:  exp(A * pi/2):"
  print '(2F8.4)', m00, m01
  print '(2F8.4)', m10, m11
end program exp_mat
```

## MATLAB / Octave
```matlab
A = [0, 1; -1, 0];
exp_At = expm(A * (pi / 2));
disp('MATLAB:   exp(A * pi/2) =');
disp(round(exp_At, 4));
```
:::
